hook: Lisa Su has led AMD since October 2014, combining an electrical-engineering research background with semiconductor operations experience to turn the company from a distant also-ran into a primary supplier of AI accelerator hardware. Her MI300 and MI400 series GPUs gave large AI labs and cloud providers a credible second source of high-end accelerators alongside Nvidia. Su holds three degrees in electrical engineering from MIT and built her career through technical and general-management roles at Texas Instruments, IBM, and Freescale Semiconductor before joining AMD in 2012. She was named Time's CEO of the Year in 2024 and continues to set AMD's AI infrastructure roadmap, from CES keynotes to plans for trillion-parameter-scale training clusters.

standing.watch: The records leave several things unresolved. The one news story on this site, the Seoul meeting with Samsung Vice Chair Jun Young-hyun over HBM and foundry partnership, has no stated outcome, so whether that discussion leads to an agreement is not settled in the records. AMD's MI400-series GPUs and the Helios rack-scale platform were announced at CES 2026, and the records mention plans for trillion-parameter-scale training clusters, but no shipment, adoption, or performance figures appear. Beyond the single 2026-10-07 story, the site holds no other coverage of Su, so any further developments in her role at AMD, her SIA chairmanship, or her advisory work are not documented here.
standing.record: The site's records on Lisa Su center on one company, AMD, where she is listed as an executive of the public company founded in 1969 and based in Santa Clara, California. Her background includes three electrical engineering degrees from MIT, a bachelor's in 1990, a master's in 1991, and a PhD in 1994, and technical and leadership roles at Texas Instruments, IBM's Semiconductor Research and Development Center, and Freescale Semiconductor before AMD. The coverage on this site amounts to a single news story, dated 2026-10-07, about her meeting Samsung Vice Chair Jun Young-hyun in Seoul to discuss HBM and foundry partnership. The pattern running through these records is a career built on semiconductor engineering and operations that now centers on positioning AMD as a supplier of AI accelerator hardware and on industry-level partnerships and policy roles.
standing.standing: Lisa Su stands as the chair and chief executive officer of AMD, a role she has held since October 2014 after joining the company in January 2012. The records show she controls AMD's AI infrastructure roadmap, including the MI300 and MI400 series GPUs that gave large AI labs and cloud providers a second source of high-end accelerators alongside Nvidia. She delivered AMD's opening keynote at CES 2026, announcing the Helios rack-scale platform and MI400-series GPUs, and the records note plans for trillion-parameter-scale training clusters. Her influence extends beyond AMD through her chairmanship of the Semiconductor Industry Association's board of directors and membership on the U.S. President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology. She was named Time's CEO of the Year in 2024 and awarded the IEEE Robert N. Noyce Medal.

quick_facts: Chair and CEO of AMD since October 2014, having joined the company in January 2012.
Earned a bachelor's degree ('90), a master's degree (SM '91), and a PhD ('94), all in electrical engineering from MIT.
Held technical and leadership roles at Texas Instruments, IBM's Semiconductor Research and Development Center, and Freescale Semiconductor before AMD.
Delivered AMD's opening keynote at CES 2026 on AI infrastructure, announcing the Helios rack-scale platform and MI400-series GPUs.
Named Time's CEO of the Year in 2024 and awarded the IEEE Robert N. Noyce Medal.
Chair of the Semiconductor Industry Association's board of directors and a member of the U.S. President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.
